issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a function named make_y_state(circ, q, p), but the template defines create_y_state(...) instead (and its NotImplementedError message references make_y_state). This name/signature mismatch will confuse students and break automated tests that call make_y_state.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function create_y_state to make_y_state and ensure its signature matches (circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float). Alternatively, add a thin wrapper make_y_state that calls create_y_state so the expected name exists and tests invoking make_y_state succeed.

issues.description: The problem statement and the reference solution use the function name make_y_state(...) for preparing a noisy |Y> resource state, but the template repository defines this stub as create_y_state(...). This mismatch means students looking for the required make_y_state implementation in the starter code will not find it, breaking the direct mapping between the task description and the template and causing confusion when wiring up subsequent functions that call make_y_state.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template stub create_y_state(...) to make_y_state(...) (or vice versa update the problem statement and solution to use create_y_state) so that the function name is consistent across the problem statement, starter code, and reference solution. Update any internal references/docs to use the unified name.
